polity_resolution.reason: The Kingdom of Saba is a historically attested South Arabian polity centered on Ma'rib. Biblical and Qur'anic traditions associate the Queen of Sheba/Saba with this polity, but no Sabaic inscription securely identifies a ruler named Bilqis.

narrative_identity_resolution.notes: Qur'an 27 narrates a woman ruling Saba but does not give her a personal name. Bilqis is the standard name in later Islamic/Arabic tradition. ATLAS therefore treats Bilqis as the legendary/traditional identity of the Queen of Sheba rather than as an epigraphically verified Sabaean monarch.

narrative_activity.traditional_context: Conventionally associated with the age of Solomon, often placed in the 10th century BCE, but this does not establish Bilqis's own accession or terminal reign boundaries.
narrative_activity.notes: The Queen of Sheba narrative presents a sovereign woman ruling Saba. The historical Kingdom of Saba is real, but Bilqis herself is not independently attested in the Sabaic epigraphic record. The conventional Solomon-era setting can be retained as narrative context only; it must not be converted into invented reign years.

authoring_contract_blocker.problem: Current executable Human Authoring requires integer Activity start and end years.
authoring_contract_blocker.model_invariant: Unknown historical boundaries must not be replaced with fake reign years merely to satisfy transitional runtime constraints.
authoring_contract_blocker.required_resolution: Support Person-only and/or unresolved-Activity authoring before compiling Bilqis into Production as a legendary Person with a traditional Saba ruling relationship.

sources.title: Queen of Sheba and Her Mighty Throne — The Unforgettable Queens of Islam
sources.use: Cambridge scholarship notes that the Qur'anic queen is not given a personal name and that Bilqis is the popular later identity attached to the Queen of Sheba tradition.

sources.title: The Queen of Sheba in Yemeni and Ethiopian Mythology — Africa and the Gulf Region
sources.use: Treats Bilqis as the Arab/Islamic Queen of Sheba figure and explicitly analyzes the narrative as mythology tied to Yemeni and Ethiopian identity.

sources.title: The Queen of Sheba Enthroned — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.use: Museum catalog identifies Bilqis with the Queen of Sheba in the later Qur'anic narrative tradition and documents her enduring traditional identity.

sources.title: The Kingdoms of Ancient Arabia — World History Foundation
sources.use: Archaeological overview establishes Saba as a real South Arabian kingdom centered on Ma'rib and distinguishes the historical kingdom from the later folklore association with Bilqis.

sources.title: 예멘의 역사를 보존하다 — National Geographic Korea
sources.use: Supports the Korean display forms 사바 왕국 and 빌키스 while describing Bilqis as the legendary ruler associated with Saba.
